opening: Punk and post-punk focus, week 4 of 4 before the Nov. 12 review: Team Dresch, Avengers, Bauhaus and TV Priest tonight.
Queens of the Stone Age, Clinic, DIIV, Ex:Re, Sennen and Thao all released albums Oct. 30.
Wilco's Being There turned 30 on Oct. 29. Johnny Cash's Unchained is dated Nov. 5, 1996 by Wikipedia and Chavez's Ride the Fader the same day (johnnycash.com lists Oct. 22: verify).
after_set_1: Perfecth is the ninth QOTSA album, on Matador, produced by Josh Homme and Michael Shuman. It has nine tracks and four singles.
Clinic's Wild in the Streets is their tenth album, on Domino. Sennen's New Quiet is their first in ten years, on Sonic Cathedral.
DIIV's ZIRP! was produced by A. G. Cook. Ex:Re is Elena Tonra of Daughter; Save As is out on 4AD.
after_set_2: Caroline Rose's Gentling the Horse at the Walt Whitman Mall came out Oct. 23 on her own label, SUCK Records, produced by John Congleton.
Philip Frobos of Omni has a solo album, Taste for the Unsavory, due Jan. 29. Mr. Dinkles, a Los Angeles duo, released Brain on Oct. 30 (one source for that date).
after_set_3: Reviewed this month and in rotation: Twisted Teens, Palace, Lex Walton, Ty Segall, This Is Lorelei, The Fall, Sylvan Esso and Yard Act.
Lex Walton's Ultimate Love Forever is out as CD and LP Nov. 20 on Sub Pop. Twisted Teens' Holy Cross Tigers is out tomorrow, Nov. 6, on Sub Pop.
Station ID at the top of the hour.
after_set_4: My Bloody Valentine's Loveless came out Nov. 4, 1991 on Creation in the UK. Teenage Fanclub's Bandwagonesque came out the same month, also on Creation.
Wilco's Being There: Oct. 29, 1996, Reprise. Johnny Cash's Unchained: Nov. 5, 1996, American Recordings, with Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers. Rusty Cage is a Soundgarden song.
The Fall's Are You Are Missing Winner came out Nov. 5, 2001 on Cog Sinister. The National's debut came out Oct. 30, 2001 (verify).
Thursday Triple Shot: Thao. Three projects: Thao & The Get Down Stay Down, Thao & Mirah, and the new single with Tune-Yards and The Linda Lindas.
Show Me is her first album in six years, out Oct. 30 on Kill Rock Stars. She plays the Independent in San Francisco Sunday, Nov. 8.
after_triple_shot: Thao & Mirah (2011) was produced by Tune-Yards' Merrill Garbus. Neko Case and Adrian Quesada guest on Show Me.
after_set_6: Tonight, Thu. Nov. 5: Team Dresch at Bottom of the Hill, The Black Angels at the Regency Ballroom, Squirrel Flower with Sour Widows at Chapel, Colleen Green at the Ivy Room in Albany.
Fri. Nov. 6: King Buffalo with L.A. Witch at the Independent. Sat. Nov. 7: Big Star Quintet at the Fillmore. Sun. Nov. 8: Thao's album release at the Independent.
after_set_7: TV Priest's Cartoons is out tomorrow, Nov. 6. Bauhaus's Passion of Lovers came out as a single in 1981, before the Mask album.
after_set_8: Numbers is from Kraftwerk's Computer World (1981). Nag, Nag, Nag is Cabaret Voltaire's 1979 Rough Trade single.
closing: Next week, Nov. 12: the last punk and post-punk week before the review.

review_rotation.window: Albums DJ Stace reviewed in the last 10 weeks (Aug. 27 to Nov. 5, 2026). All 13 were posted Oct. 4 to 15; no new reviews on Zookeeper since.
review_rotation.rule: Tapering: weeks 1 to 3 after review, one track per album per show; weeks 4 to 6, about half the albums per show; weeks 7 to 10, about one in four. Pick five-star, FCC-clean tracks not aired in the past 21 days.
review_rotation.this_show: Week 4 for the 10 albums reviewed Oct. 4 to 8: five of them play (Twisted Teens Blame the Clown, Palace, Lex Walton, Ty Segall, This Is Lorelei). Week 3 for The Fall, Sylvan Esso and Yard Act: one track each. 8 tracks. Resting this week: Twisted Teens Florida Water Blues, Dread Spectre Council, Little Barrie, Sluice and Tricky. The tracks Stace cut Oct. 29 (Overhead, Dream On, Ultimate Love 4Ever, Hand Me A Cigarette, I Still See Me There, Billy Came Back, Retro Song, Flood Season, You're Gonna Need A Little Music, Hex's Up) are avoided; other tracks from the same albums stand in.
